websiteObservations: Modern site, works well on a phone, decent photography, clear enquiry form and prices for design consultations. Genuinely well put together — there is no obvious problem to solve here.

research.summary: Landscaping and garden design company with a strong online presence: a good modern website, active Instagram, well-maintained Google profile and a booked-up schedule. Included deliberately as an example of a prospect where the honest answer is that there is no opportunity — the tool should help you qualify out politely rather than push.
observations: Website is modern, fast and works properly on mobile
Enquiry form and consultation pricing already on the site
Instagram is active and the photography is good
Google profile is complete and reviewed recently
problems: No obvious problem — this is the point of including them
At most, they may be booked up and not looking for more work
opportunities: Very little. Possibly a conversation in future if they expand
Worth a short, respectful call and a clean exit
talkingPoints: Tell them honestly that their site is already doing its job
Ask once whether they're looking for more work — if not, leave it
A professional exit here is the right outcome
notes: EXAMPLE DATASET — written to demonstrate the tool, not researched

script.opening: Hi, is that Priya? It's Ollie from NexalField. Quick one and I'll be honest with you — I ring local businesses about their websites, and yours is already one of the better ones I've seen, so this might be a short call. Have you got twenty seconds?
script.hook: I build websites for local businesses around KT2. Normally I'm ringing because there's something obviously missing — in your case there isn't, so the only thing worth asking is whether you're looking to take on more work at the minute or whether you're comfortable as you are.
script.valueStatement: Honestly, your site's doing its job. The only thing I'd ever look at for a business like yours is whether the enquiries coming in are the right kind of work rather than just more of it — and that's a different conversation to the one I usually have.
